A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GI-GS framework and retain directly matchable methods and experiments. Text, equations, tables, figures, and all appendices are readable, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original GI-GS results for novel-view synthesis, material estimation, relighting, and ablations on TensoIR and Mip-NeRF 360, including supplementary results.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and adds experiments on Synthetic4Relight and Stanford-ORB, along with new normal-estimation, illumination, and relighting analyses.

M1.justification: The core pipeline and losses remain intact, but Equation 12 changes the reported ray-intersection condition from zd < z to zd < z < zd + delta. V2 also demonstrates optional adaptations using Omnidata normal supervision, point-light shadow maps, and Monte Carlo relighting in Appendices E, F.5, and J. These are localized extensions rather than a replacement of GI-GS.

E1.justification: Appendix I adds Synthetic4Relight objects and four real-object Stanford-ORB scenes to the retained TensoIR and Mip-NeRF 360 coverage. Appendix F.5 also demonstrates point-light relighting, extending the previously demonstrated environment-map illumination scenarios.

E2.justification: V2 adds vanilla 3DGS to the TensoIR per-object comparison in Table 8, includes PhySG* in Table 10, and adds TensoIR to the explicit occlusion comparison in Figure 16. Existing comparator sets in Tables 1–7 remain unchanged; extending GS-IR to additional datasets does not itself constitute another comparator addition.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce Omnidata-supervised controls, paired ray-marching settings of 0.05/8 steps and 0.1/16 steps, and roughness MSE evaluation. Appendix J separately tests ground-truth albedo rescaling, environment-energy normalization, color-gamut correction, and Monte Carlo rendering. These expand the evaluation design; the stated training schedules and metrics for the original experiments remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained occlusion/indirect-lighting and ray-count ablations, v2 adds material-estimation and relighting ablations in Table 9, normal-supervision comparisons, path-tracing sensitivity examples, a sharp-shadow case study, component decompositions, and relighting-normalization analysis. These directly investigate additional mechanisms and failure conditions.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for the experimental results. V2 continues to present point estimates and qualitative comparisons without introducing uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: All pre-existing numerical entries in Tables 1–8 are retained. V2 adds training times for more baselines, 3DGS TensoIR scores, and substantial new ablation and benchmark results in Tables 9–11. For example, Table 11 reports Stanford-ORB average relighting PSNR of 28.54 for GI-GS versus 25.31 for GS-IR. These are added results, not improvements to the original same-setting scores.

T1.justification: Appendix F.2 adds Equation 29, deriving the specular-direction residual introduced when first-pass RGB substitutes for indirect incident radiance. Equation 12 also revises the formal visibility condition through the thickness bound. The remaining rendering derivations are retained, without a substantial new theoretical framework or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract changes the relighting characterization to competitive, and the conclusion replaces the broad state-of-the-art claim across rendering and relighting tasks with superior novel-view synthesis against inverse-rendering methods and comparable relighting with greater efficiency. The three central contributions remain unchanged.

C2.justification: New appendices explain the specular approximation error, false ray intersections, difficulty producing sharp directional shadows, and the effects of normal accuracy and relighting normalization. Appendix H also explains different albedo artifacts caused by omitting occlusion or indirect illumination. These substantially expand the mechanism explanations and applicability boundaries beyond v1's retained limitations paragraph.

D1.justification: V2 supplies concrete ray-marching configurations in Figure 19, describes the additional supervision and relighting procedures, and discloses how the constructed reference images in Figures 27–28 are produced. The project-page address changes. Appendix A's hardware, iteration counts, learning rates, and loss weights remain unchanged; the new material does not provide a comprehensive replacement implementation specification.

R1.justification: V2 adds references to Omnidata and Stanford-ORB and expands discussion of existing works through NeILF's Fibonacci sampling and TensoIR's occlusion and relighting procedures. The main related-work account and the central distinction from baked indirect-lighting approaches remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Related-work and preliminary subsections become run-in headings, several method and results paragraphs are tightened, and the abstract and conclusion are revised. Appendices E–K extend the analytical organization, but most existing prose and the main narrative sequence are preserved rather than extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: Figure 1 moves before the abstract, and existing figures and tables are resized and rearranged. Table 1 gains a timing column and Table 8 gains 3DGS rows. New Tables 9–11 and Figures 14–31 add substantial comparison grids, diagnostic visualizations, and explanatory diagrams while retaining the original figures.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens validation of material estimation and relighting through additional synthetic and real-object evaluations, targeted ablations, and studies of normal accuracy and rendering settings. It also explains approximation failures and narrows the overstated relighting conclusion. These address important evidential and explanatory gaps in v1. Some additions require caution: Figures 27–28 use method-dependent constructed relighting references, and Table 10 contradicts the blanket lower-LPIPS claim for relighting. These localized weaknesses limit particular comparisons but do not outweigh the broader improvement in diagnostic evidence and transparency.
